(2026-09-22, hv's selection in the TUI vc asked, recorded at 2026-09-22T16:12:18Z by vc's clock; wording vc's, the choice hv's; vc's recommendation taken) A BOARD MAY CLAIM AN ISSUE, IN THE FORM `ISSUE:0512`, AND THE WIDENING IS NOT ONE-SIDED. `is_claim_address` (model.rs) admits only ST0079 and ST0079/01 and never calls `is_issue_id`, which has existed unused beside it, so `claims:` is empty BY CONSTRUCTION for exactly the work that fills the time between releases -- and it is therefore silent precisely where two concurrent sessions would collide. The live case is the afternoon this was ruled: four nodes were dispatched onto four different issues and not one could say so on its board. THE SPELLING IS THE MANIFEST'S OWN, not a new one: `organize --default` writes `ISSUE:<NNNN>` per OPEN issue into `intent/.intentfiles` and this repository's own manifest carries them, so the system already records this address kind elsewhere and refused it only at this door. THE SECOND HALF, WHICH THE ISSUE BODY DOES NOT CARRY AND WHICH VC MEASURED BEFORE ASKING: `renumber::issue` deliberately rewrites NOTHING, on the stated ground that "nothing structured refers to an issue -- `related` and claims both name threads -- so the only references it can have are prose". Admitting issue claims FALSIFIES that sentence, so `issues renumber` must gain the claim-rewriting `renumber::thread` already has, or a renumber silently leaves a board claiming a number that moved; the comment stating the old reason is part of the change rather than a leftover. `moved_claims` is the implementation to copy, so the cost is bounded. WHAT WAS REFUSED AND WHY: free-text claims, because two claims could then be compared only by string equality and the field would stop answering the collision question it exists for; and the bare `0512` form, because the manifest already writes the prefixed one and two spellings of one address is the drift Highlander names, while saving nothing -- it carries the same renumber consequence either way.

(2026-09-22, hv's selections in the TUI vc asked, recorded at 2026-09-22T17:29:22Z by vc's clock; wording vc's, each choice hv's; vc's recommendation taken on both) TWO RULINGS ON THE DEPLOYMENT PAIR, 0517 AND 0518. (1) A STALE DELIVERED PAIR IS REFUSED AT **PUSH**, NOT AT COMMIT AND NOT AT EVERY INVOCATION. The pre-push hook refuses when the pair's embedded commit is behind HEAD. The decisive evidence against the cheap option is that THE CHEAP OPTION HAS ALREADY BEEN TRIED AND FAILED: the pre-commit gate's `self-provenance: currency` arm already REPORTS this, in full, on every commit, and four nodes and vc read past it for an entire afternoon while two judged and landed fixes -- 0509's and 0513's -- ran in no estate on the machine. A push is a batch boundary and is hv's own hand, so one `build all` covers every Rust change since the last push, the refusal reaches the person who can act on it, and it cannot fire inside a node's judging run. Refusing at COMMIT was rejected because it forces a heavy rebuild, which has no dry run, between every bank and its landing; a WRAPPER on `~/.local/bin/intent` was rejected because it puts latency and a new failure mode in front of every tool call in every estate, including the hooks that run `intent` in every Claude session. (2) 0517 CLOSES AS RECORDED, WITH THE PROTOCOL AS ITS REMEDY: all `lib/templates/` work is built in a DETACHED WORKTREE, which is the only containment, because the install root pointer file contains this tree's path and THE AUTHOR'S SAVE IS THE DEPLOYMENT -- a hold on such a bank controls the record and not the running behaviour. Repointing the install root at a committed copy was rejected as the 2026-09-19 `publish_home` incident, where a scratch tree's root reached every estate's gate for hours; and the save-is-deployment property is deliberate and useful, since a template fix reaches every estate at once. THE HONEST COST, RECORDED RATHER THAN SOFTENED: this rests on discipline, and discipline failed twice on 2026-09-22 -- dc landed across a halt twice in one day. What makes it survivable is that the blast-radius check moved to the FRONT of judging for this directory, since it is the only thing bounding live-but-unjudged bytes while a suite is owed.
